extracted.intended_audience: general readers and scholars using the Project Gutenberg eBook of Alexander von Humboldt's Cosmos (readers of natural philosophy, translators, and eBook distributors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and implied standards for composing a 'physical description of the universe' (Cosmos) — covering scope, method, style, empirical grounding, and translation/distribution practices. Also includes Project Gutenberg distribution requirements for the eBook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim: comprehensive physical description of the universe
rubrics_metrics.description: The work is 'intended ... to embrace a summary of physical knowledge, as connected with a delineation of the material universe.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover both celestial and terrestrial phenomena across the full domain of 'Cosmos' rather than a narrow specialty; the finished project is envisioned as three volumes addressing complementary aspects (summary of phenomena, incitements to study nature and history of contemplation, and the special scientific development).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct parts, each self-contained
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the three parts of the Cosmos is 'to a certain extent, distinct in its object, and may be considered complete in itself.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the work so individual volumes/parts can stand alone on their stated objectives while contributing to the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity and connection of phenomena (holistic treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent nature 'as one great whole, moved and animated by internal forces' and seek 'insight into the connection of phenomena as the aim of all natural investigation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize reciprocal dependence among scientific disciplines; avoid isolated, disconnected facts — instead show how special departments fructify one another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical grounding and citation of authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever possible the author has 'adduced the authorities from whence I derived my facts, with a view of affording testimony both to the accuracy of my statements and to the value of the observations to which reference was made.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sources for facts, indicate direct quotations, and prefer original editions for accuracy (especially for numerical data). Cited authorities support accuracy and allow verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for exact quotation over paraphrase
rubrics_metrics.description: In extracting short passages from friends' works 'I have indicated them by marks of quotation; and, in imitation of the practice of the ancients, I have invariably preferred the repetition of the same words to any arbitrary substitution of my own paraphrases.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reproducing others' language, preserve original wording where feasible rather than paraphrasing, to retain precision of expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific completeness balanced with picturesque, life-like style
rubrics_metrics.description: A certain degree of 'scientific completeness in the treatment of individual facts is not wholly incompatible with a picturesque animation of style.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dry enumerations or exhaustive lists that produce a wearying impression; aim for life-like truthfulness and vivid, animated description while retaining scientific rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mere encyclopedic enumeration; favour general views
rubrics_metrics.description: Misunderstood popular knowledge may confound cosmography with 'a mere encyclopedic enumeration of natural sciences.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on connecting generalities and specialties and on providing interpretive, synthetic perspectives rather than producing only an encyclopedia-style compilation of disconnected facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method and limits of exposition (organization and starting point)
rubrics_metrics.description: The delineation 'begins with the laws of gravitation, and with the region of the remotest nebulous spots and double stars, and then, gradually descending through the starry stratum ... contemplates this terrestrial spheroid ... and finally ... the geography of organic forms.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and state the limits and method of the work up front; adopt a clear organizational order (Humboldt recommends starting with celestial phenomena and descending to terrestrial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of observation, experiment, induction and empirical laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Empiricism and experiments lead, 'by analogy and induction, to a knowledge of 'empirical laws'; their gradual simplification and generalization.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base claims on observed phenomena and experiments; use induction to derive empirical laws and simplify/generalize results; avoid speculative claims unsupported by evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative emphasis where appropriate ('mean numerical values')
rubrics_metrics.description: Amid mobile elements 'mean numerical values' are 'the ultimate aim of investigation, being the expression of the physical laws, or forces of the Cosmos.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numerical measurements and comparative data (e.g., hypsometrical/elevation data, densities, periods) to express physical laws; be careful with numerical accuracy and units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in numerical relations; prefer original editions for numerical data
rubrics_metrics.description: When quoting from his own writings 'I have always referred to the original editions, owing to the importance of accuracy with regard to numerical relations, and to my own distrust of the care and correctness of translators.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify numerical data against primary sources; translators/authors should check original editions to avoid transcription/translation errors in numbers and measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not omit passages for national prejudices; preserve completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Translator notes he 'have not conceived myself justified in omitting passages, sometimes amounting to pages, simply because they might be deemed slightly obnoxious to our national prejudices.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain fidelity and completeness in translation/publication; do not excise material merely because it might be controversial or culturally uncomfortable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid disputes about priority (minimize contentious claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'much-contested question of priority of claim to a first discovery ... has rarely been touched upon.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, refrain from dwelling on claims of priority; focus on exposition and synthesis rather than priority controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use public lectures as a test of exposition (iterative drafting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public lectures 'seemed to me to present an easy and efficient means of testing the more or less successful manner of connecting together the detached branches of any one science.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test organization and clarity by presenting material orally or to peers before finalizing text, using feedback to improve connections among topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translator's standards: accuracy, completeness, and unit conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Translator's Preface: this translation 'differ from those of Mrs. Sabine in having all the foreign measures converted into corresponding English terms, in being published at considerably less than one third of the price, and in being a translation of the entire work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For translations aimed at a target readership, convert measures to familiar units for clarity, keep translation complete, and prioritize both accuracy and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope checklist: include celestial and terrestrial topics listed in contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Contents enumerate a wide range of topics (e.g., celestial phenomena, planetary systems, comets, aerolites, zodiacal light; terrestrial topics such as figure of the earth, density, internal heat, magnetism, geognostic phenomena, volcanoes, rocks, paleontology, meteorology, climatology, geography of plants and animals, man and races).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the work covers the major subject domains Humboldt lists when aiming to produce a comprehensive 'Cosmos' — treat celestial systems, planetary science, terrestrial geognosy, atmosphere and climate, and biogeography in appropriate depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include authorities/notes and numerical appendices where useful
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes appended (e.g., hypsometrical data, measurements, chemical composition of meteoric asteroids) are used to provide supporting numerical and specialized detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide notes and appendices for technical data and detailed measurements instead of interrupting the main narrative flow; use notes for specialized supporting material.
